components.name: Live Rain trend
components.description: A live weather trend at the wide-card 72px plot height. Rain mixes dusk blue (Pressure: pale gold) equally with gray-9 for the line and uses the chart color at 8% for the band; unavailable or disabled trends fall back to the dashed gray treatment.

narrative.overview:
Hearth is a quiet, dark-only household workspace: true black ground, untinted gray structure, and small deliberate signals of voice, action, and freshness. Readings and their evidence lead; ornament stays subordinate to the work.

The household workspace is spacious enough to read at a glance. Development pages use the same tokens and controls at a higher information density. Follow [GLOSSARY.md](GLOSSARY.md): State, Entity availability, and Command outcome are distinct facts, not interchangeable status labels.
keyCharacteristics: True black ground with a numbered, neutral gray ramp.
Violet for Hearth's voice; orange for the primary action and arrival signals.
A changed reading arrives as an afterglow: the card's top edge lights orange and fades over ten seconds. Text states each reading's age and availability.
A shared reading scale with a narrow-card step; compact diagnostics share the same tokens.
One card frame and one state table for every data card in a view.

rules.name: The One Action Rule
rules.body: Reserve orange for the primary action and the afterglow on a changed reading. Charts and trends draw no now marker: the time axis ends at the window's end. Use outline controls for filters, pagination, and secondary actions. Disabled primary actions become gray, not dimmed orange.

rules.name: The Evidence Rule
rules.body: The afterglow marks newer data that changed what a card shows. It says nothing about a reading's age, Entity availability, or Command outcome; text states those. Never rely on brand color alone to communicate status.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Surfaces at rest cast no shadow. Only the overlays above the workspace use one: the modal, popovers, and drawers.

rules.name: The One Focus Ring Rule
rules.body: Every focusable control shows the same 2px violet outline with a 3px offset, from the global `:focus-visible` rule. A component may move the ring to the part that takes input, as the brightness slider does with its thumb, but never restyles it.

rules.name: The Stable Height Rule
rules.body: Feedback never moves the layout. Each control reserves its status line while idle, so a Command that settles in milliseconds doesn't move the card. Opening Source never changes a card's or a grid row's height. A message longer than the reserved line grows the card only while it shows, and Cover tiles never grow.

rules.name: The One Frame Rule
rules.body: Every data card in a view uses one frame. Future card types follow this contract rather than copying an existing card.

dos: Do use the neutral gray ramp for surfaces and preserve true black as the ground.
Do pair arrival, status, and availability signals with explicit text.
Do use violet for Hearth's voice and orange for the main action and arrival signals.
Do use the defined reading scales and outline buttons for filters and paging.
Do use glossary terms precisely when presenting State, availability, and Command outcomes.
Do reserve a control's status line while idle, so feedback never moves the card.
Do give household controls a 44px target on touch.
Do build a new data card on the shared card frame and card states.
donts: Don't turn orange into a series color or a disabled brown primary button.
Don't tint the neutral gray ramp or replace status colors with brand hues.
Don't use the afterglow for anything but a changed reading: not age, availability, or successful Commands.
Don't use broad decorative gradients or depend on color alone for meaning.
Don't draw a radial gauge or a now marker.
